title: See the unmatched terminal
statement:
What makes CH₂Cl₂ polar even though its carbon has tetrahedral geometry?

[_]{a}

choices: The bond dipoles do not sum to zero.
Every bond has the same polarity.
explanations: The molecular substitutions break full tetrahedral cancellation.
All four carbon domains are bonds.
Carbon’s four bonding domains are tetrahedral.
The two terminal element types give different bond dipoles.

hints: Draw a tetrahedral arrangement with two H and two Cl.
Identical bonds would cancel in a tetrahedral molecule.
Here C–Cl vectors are not opposite and the terminal pairs differ.
solution: Draw a tetrahedral arrangement with two H and two Cl. Identical bonds would cancel in a tetrahedral molecule. Here C–Cl vectors are not opposite and the terminal pairs differ. The molecular substitutions break full tetrahedral cancellation.
